column1: # Measured impact of widening rdo_cfl_alpha's search (removed the `count < alpha` early-exit,
# making the +/-16 alpha search exhaustive). Tried as lever #3 in docs/RD_GAP_VS_LIBAOM.md after
# zenrav1e#26 (extended partition types) hit an unresolved conformance bug. RULED OUT -- reverted,
# not on master.
# Harness: scripts/rd_gap/run_gap.sh, cavif -s2, 22-image photo corpus, 12-point Q grid, same
# methodology as the topdown-fix measurement. "fixed" = topdown+deblock fixes only (665e58e4 +
# dc0a1165, master's actual state); "cflwide" = fixed + the reverted CfL change.
# Direct cflwide-vs-fixed (isolates the CfL change; no libaom involved), bpp change at matched
# ssim2, + = cflwide needs MORE bits (worse):
target_ssim2
# Against the same-day libaom baseline (fixed vs cflwide, both merged with the same libaom rows):
condition
fixed_vs_libaom (baseline, master's actual state)
cflwide_vs_libaom
# CONCLUSION: noise-level, no consistent direction, slightly negative in aggregate. Root cause:
# rdo_cfl_alpha optimizes SSE only ("We're not doing RDO here" per the code's own comment) --
# widening the search sometimes finds a lower-SSE alpha that costs MORE BITS to signal
# (cfl:alpha_u/v entropy cost scales with |alpha|), producing a worse RD outcome despite lower
# distortion. This is not simply "search deeper == better" for a distortion-only inner loop whose
# result feeds an outer RD comparison. Reverted (increased encode time for zero measured benefit).
# A REAL fix here would need to make the alpha search RD-aware (rate-aware, not SSE-only), which
# is a different, larger change than "widen the search range" -- not attempted.
